user.title: Set up a KWB heater
user.description: Choose a name and connection type for your KWB heater. Enter its nominal power to estimate heat output and pellet consumption. Adjust the pellet properties and efficiency to match your installation.

data_description.name: Used for the device and its sensor names, for example, Basement heater.
data_description.type: Choose Serial for a device connected directly to the Home Assistant host, or TCP for a serial-to-Ethernet server.
data_description.nominal_power: Rated thermal output from the heater nameplate in kW. Default: 25 kW. Must be greater than 0. Editable on the device after setup.
data_description.pellet_bulk_density: Mass of one liter of loose pellets, including the spaces between pellets. Default: 0.65 kg/L. Must be greater than 0. Converts estimated consumption from kg/h to L/h. Editable on the device after setup.
data_description.boiler_efficiency: Boiler efficiency as a percentage. Default: 95%. Enter 95 for 95%, not 0.95. Must be greater than 0 and at most 100. Used with nominal power and pellet energy density to estimate consumption. Editable on the device after setup.
data_description.pellet_energy: Energy content from your pellet supplier in kWh/kg. Default: 4.8 kWh/kg. Must be greater than 0. Use the same lower or higher heating-value basis as the boiler efficiency. Used with nominal power and efficiency to estimate consumption. Editable on the device after setup.
data_description.pellet_price: Price of 1 metric ton (1,000 kg) of pellets in your Home Assistant currency. Default: 0. Must be zero or greater. Editable on the device after setup. Changing the price recalculates the cost of the entire recorded consumption total.

serial.title: Serial connection

data_description.device: For example, /dev/ttyUSB0. Prefer a persistent /dev/serial/by-id/ path so the connection remains valid after a restart.
data_description.raw: Expose raw packet sensors for troubleshooting. Leave this disabled for normal use.

serial.description: Enter the serial device path as seen by Home Assistant.

tcp.title: TCP connection
tcp.description: Enter the network address and TCP port of the serial-to-Ethernet server connected to your heater.

data_description.host: For example, 192.168.1.50 or boiler.local. Enter only the hostname or IP address, without a URL scheme or port.
data_description.port: The serial server’s TCP listening port (1–65535). The default is 23; use the port configured on your server.
data_description.raw: Expose raw packet sensors for troubleshooting. Leave this disabled for normal use.

error.cannot_connect: Unable to connect. For serial, check the device path and Home Assistant’s access to the device. For TCP, check the host, port, and network connection.

abort.already_configured: This heater connection is already configured.
abort.already_in_progress: Setup for this heater connection is already in progress.
